title: AnyOfFalseBranchRoot
description: Issue #133's second table. A `false` branch states neither a required key nor a property check, so the object-shape summary dropped the whole "at least one branch matches" assertion and {"j":"b"} was accepted on the strength of the one branch written to reject everything. Nothing escapes the merged struct through a `false` branch, so the struct stays and the applicator is evaluated against the document instead.
